stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Adjust the accelerating voltage $U$ and the magnetic field $B$, then press FIRE. Watch how the ion's circular radius $R$ responds. Try at least two values of $U$ and move $B$.
stages.concept: Acceleration sets the ion's speed: $v = \sqrt{2\,q\,U/m}$. In the perpendicular magnetic field, the Lorentz force curves the ion into a circle of radius $R = m\,v/(q\,B) = \sqrt{2\,U\,m/q}\,/\,B$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three detector cells are labelled with target ion masses. Fire each ion so that it lands on its own cell. The dashed preview arc shows where the current $(U, B)$ sends the loaded ion — line it up, then FIRE.
stages.concept: Solved for the settings: $B = \sqrt{2\,U\,m/q}\,/\,R$ or $U = q\,B^{2}\,R^{2}/(2\,m)$. Two ions of different mass with the same $(U, B)$ separate because $R \propto \sqrt{m}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview arc. For each ion you get exactly one shot. Read the loaded mass $m$ and its target radius $R$, calculate $(U, B)$ on paper, dial them in, then FIRE. Miss the budget and the bench resets.
stages.concept: Isolate the mass: $m = q\,B^{2}\,R^{2}/(2\,U)$. This is the identification equation of the mass spectrograph — the deflection radius $R$ is the observable that reveals $m$ once $U$, $B$, and $q$ are fixed.

labels.tip1: change U, move B, then FIRE
labels.tip2: use the preview arc to route each ion to its labelled cell
labels.tip3: compute U and B from m and target R, then FIRE
labels.peek_tip_scaling: R is proportional to sqrt(m). If two cells sit at radii R1 and R2, their masses satisfy m1/m2 = (R1/R2)^2 for one shared (U, B).
labels.peek_tip_solve_b: Fix U at a comfortable value, then solve B = sqrt(2 U m / q) / R. Small B = large radius; big B = tight radius.
labels.peek_tip_solve_u: Fix B at a comfortable value, then solve U = q B^2 R^2 / (2 m). Higher mass at the same cell needs less U.

1.1: Move the U slider (right) and the B slider (left) and fire between changes.
1.2: R grows with sqrt(U) and shrinks as B increases — check by doubling one at a time.
1.3: For the same ion, R = sqrt(2 U m / q) / B: same R has many (U, B) solutions.

2.1: Each cell is labelled with the mass of its ion. Aim the preview arc at that cell for the loaded ion.
2.2: Solve for one setting: B = sqrt(2 U m / q) / R with U fixed, or U = q B^2 R^2 / (2 m) with B fixed.
2.3: The loaded ion cycles through the queue automatically — hit one, the next mass loads.

3.1: Write down m and R for the loaded ion. Pick a sensible U, solve for B (or vice versa).
3.2: Rearrange R = sqrt(2 U m / q) / B into m = q B^2 R^2 / (2 U); use it to double-check your (U, B).
3.3: Watch the ratio: for two ions in the same setup, R1/R2 = sqrt(m1/m2). One (U, B) can hit both if their cells respect that ratio.
